title: xAI MCP: How to Connect MCP Servers and Tools (2026)
summary: xAI MCP provides remote tool integration for Grok through the API. Understand the costs, how it works, and what limitations apply.
body_markdown:
## XAI MCP is remote tool access for Grok


### The short answer


**Nobody sells "xAI MCP"** , and there is no switch to turn it on.


It's xAI's support for the Model Context Protocol in its API, which lets a Grok model such as Grok 4.7 call tools hosted on a remote server, whether that's one you built yourself or one from a platform like[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) .


[Nodeflare](https://nodeflare.tech/blog/github-mcp-server-token-usage) checked this against docs.x.ai on 17 November 2026. Read the docs page for the current request format, because parameter names are the part of an integration that gets edited without notice.


### What MCP is, independent of xAI


A model needs some way to discover and call external tools, and the Model Context Protocol is the open standard for that. A server publishes a list of tools, each with a name, a description and an input schema.


A client reads that list and sends calls back.


Because the contract is the same everywhere, a server written once serves any client that speaks the protocol.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) shows the payoff: a integration connected there is both a step in a flow and a tool on the project's MCP server, so each of its 750 integrations is something Grok can call without a second catalogue to publish or re-integrate.


The action behind both is the same one in packages/integrations in the open source repo.


Follow the request through the picture below. An application sends it to the xAI API, Grok decides a tool is needed, and the call goes out to a remote MCP server. That server sits outside xAI and fronts the data, ticketing and CRM tools.


### What xAI MCP is not


It's not a catalogue of ready-made connectors, so nothing is pre-wired to your ticketing system or CRM. **It's not a hosted server either** : xAI doesn't run the tools for you.


Whatever access you grant to the server, Grok's calls inherit it, because xAI MCP isn't a free-standing permission layer.


And **it isn't exempt from billing** , because a tool call is still a model request that you pay for.
